summary: 48-foot Aermotor lookout on Bernheim Forest, built 1929 and staffed until 1980; open to visitors on set days. Register and arboretum differ on the builder.

facts.design: 48-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab

access.note: Open on set days: usually summer weekends when weather permits, spring and fall school breaks, and extra fall days; call ahead for schedule changes

visit.trail_note: Visitors can go up to the top; the arboretum asks people to call ahead for last-minute schedule changes

events.note: Constructed 1929; arboretum says Mr. Bernheim directed the build; register credits the Kentucky Division of Forestry
Regularly staffed until 1980; trained observers in small planes took over
Used to monitor a wildfire in 1986

corrections.why: Both the NHLR entry and the arboretum's own page date construction to 1929
Arboretum says the tower is usually open on summer weekends and during school breaks, and that visitors can go to the top

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the Kentucky Division of Forestry constructed the tower in 1929. The arboretum says Mr. Bernheim directed that it be built and that the state's help began in the mid-1950s with a radio. The story reports both. Both give 1929.

The arboretum history says Mr. Bernheim bought the land in 1928 and endowed it in 1929. Nature's Notebook says the tower came the year after the purchase and also says he purchased the land in 1929. The story gives the 1928 and 1929 readings and does not settle the year.

NHLR lists the site at 887 ft (270 m). The arboretum gives the knob as 921 ft above sea level and the tower top as about 969 ft. The record keeps 270.4 m from NHLR. The tower-top figure is not used in facts.

sources.title: Bernheim at 90: Happy Birthday to our historic fire tower
Nature's Notebook: A View from the Firetower

notes_for_editor: Builder credit is unresolved between the register and the arboretum; the story presents both. Purchase year (1928 vs 1929) is left open. Access and visit facts come from the arboretum's own page, which is undated in the fetch; hours change, so recheck before publishing. Height 48 ft converted to 14.6 m. Record's 270.4 m elevation matches NHLR site height; not the tower top. The brief's record had no built event; proposed 1929. No photos added; the arboretum mentions a 1931 photo of I.W. Bernheim at the tower but no image URL was read. Two web searches returned arboretum pages and no Kentucky Division of Forestry page.
